title: Mutual Information
interviewAnswer: Mutual information measures how much knowing one variable reduces uncertainty about another and can capture nonlinear dependence.
why: MI connects probability, feature selection and representation learning.
intuition: If knowing X says nothing about Y, MI is zero; if X nearly determines Y, shared information is large.
deepDive: I(X;Y)=D_KL(p(x,y)||p(x)p(y))=H(X)-H(X|Y). Estimating MI in high-dimensional continuous data is difficult and estimator-dependent.
commonMistakes: Assuming zero correlation means zero MI.
Comparing biased MI estimators as if values were directly comparable.
production: Use MI-based features carefully: leakage can look like strong information.
workedExample: Y=X² can have weak linear correlation for symmetric X while still having substantial MI.
